title: Contributor Access & Growth Charter: role boarding, benefits alignment, and tools gateway
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This charter defines the end-to-end process we call "Contributor Boarding & Growth": how new joiners and role changers at Redwood receive the right benefits, training, and tool access; how role ladders and skill badges are aligned to operational requirements; and the SLA-driven responsibilities for People Ops, IT, and Team Leads. The goal is to reduce time-to-productivity, remove ad-hoc exceptions, and surface measurable signals for career progression and benefits eligibility.

Who this document is for
- People Ops and Hiring Managers
- Engineering and Product Team Leads
- IT and SRE who manage provisioning pipelines
- New joiners and internal transferees
- Security & Compliance reviewers

Scope
This charter covers:
- Role boarding (new hires and internal role changes)
- Core benefits enrollment windows and eligibility triggers
- Tooling and IAM access request flows for the first 90 days
- Role ladder mapping to required trainings and badge criteria
- Ownership, SLAs, and escalation paths

Principles
1) Minimal friction: routine provisioning completes automatically where policy allows.
2) Safety by default: least-privilege access until role verification is completed.
3) Visibility and auditability: all changes are traceable and linked to role events.
4) Career-first: access and benefits support skills growth and measurable milestones.

Key definitions
- Role Boarding: the combined steps that move a person from offer acceptance to fully provisioned contributor in a role.
- Role Badge: a lightweight credential attached to a profile that signifies completion of role-specific training/skills.
- Active Tools: tools required for day-to-day work (e.g., code repo, CI, cloud console).

Role Boarding: step-by-step process (owners at each step)
1. Offer accepted (People Ops)
   - Trigger: candidate accepts offer in HRIS.
   - Action: People Ops issues welcome email + first-day checklist.
   - SLA: within 2 business hours of acceptance.
2. Account skeleton creation (IT automation)
   - Create SSO account and corporate email alias.
   - Provision baseline access group: "new-contributor" (calendar, docs, Slack read, knowledge base).
   - SLA: within 6 hours.
3. Benefits enrollment window (People Ops)
   - Open enrollment link and benefits package summary emailed.
   - New joiner has 30 calendar days to enroll for medical, 60 days for commuter/other plans where applicable.
   - SLA notification: day 1 and day 21 reminders.
4. Role-specific access requests (Hiring Manager + IT)
   - Hiring Manager submits Role Access Form (RAF) in the onboarding portal listing required services, environments, and privilege levels.
   - IT applies least-privilege defaults; advanced privileges require People Ops + Team Lead sign-off.
   - SLA: RAF processed within 24 hours for non-sensitive services, 72 hours for production privileges.
5. First-week ramp and training (Team Lead)
   - Assign buddy and schedule core training: security baseline, infra intro, codebase walkthrough.
   - Complete Role Acceptance checklist in People Ops system.
   - Expected outcome: contributor can run local dev and submit first PR by EOD week 1 for IC roles.
6. Badge nomination and verification (Team Lead + People Ops)
   - After 60 days, Team Lead nominates for role badge if criteria met (see badge table).
   - Badge issuance triggers expanded tool access (if applicable) and benefit eligibility where policy ties benefits to role level.

Role Ladder & Skill Badging (overview)
The role ladder is intentionally modular: base role, intermediate skill badges, and level anchors. Badges are listed and mapped to measurable criteria below. Badges are additive and portable across teams.

Badge table (human-readable)
- Badge name | Who awards | Criteria (examples) | Typical timeline
- Core Dev Ready | Team Lead | Completed local dev setup, first PR merged, security baseline training | 1–2 weeks
- System Owner | Team Lead + SRE | Can deploy to staging, passed runbook review, incident playbook demo | 60–90 days
- Data-Driven Feature | Product + Eng | Completed product analytics course, shipped metric-backed feature | 90–180 days
- Mentor & Onboarder | People Ops + Manager | Completed mentor training, onboarded >=2 contributors | 6–12 months

Note: Badge criteria must be documented on the role profile page; Teams can add optional badges.

Benefits alignment & eligibility matrix (summary table)
- Benefit | Eligibility trigger | Enrollment window | Admin owner
- Health insurance | Onboarding complete & in-payroll | 30 days | People Ops
- Retirement match | Payroll active & 3-month tenure | Immediate enrollment; vesting applies | Finance/Payroll
- Parental leave top-up | Role level L3+ or equivalent | Apply 30 days before leave | People Ops
- Education stipend | Badge: Mentor & Onboarder OR approval | Quarterly application cycle | People Ops

Tooling access rules and examples
- Baseline (new-contributor): Slack, Docs, Internal Wiki read, GitHub read, CI status.
- Developer-level: Git push, internal CI job triggers, dev cloud accounts (staging).
- Production-level: limited to Service Account access and controlled via Just-In-Time (JIT) requests and audit.

Provisioning examples (CLI snippets and templates)
1) Role Access Form (RAF) template (example fields):
   - candidate_name: string
   - role: string
   - team: string
   - required_services: list (e.g., repoA:write, cloudX:staging-deploy)
   - production_access_needed: boolean
   - manager_approval: boolean

2) Sample IAM request command (developer-facing):
   - rcli iam request --user maya.chen@redwood.com --role dev --services repoA:write,cloud-staging:deploy --reason "onboard:feature-x"

Access matrix (text table)
- Role | Baseline | Developer | Staging | Production | Badge uplift
- IC1 | Y | Y (limited) | N | N | Core Dev Ready -> staging Y
- IC2 | Y | Y | Y | JIT only | System Owner -> production JIT
- Manager | Y | Y | Y | JIT only | Manager approvals required

Ownership & SLAs
- People Ops: manages offer, benefits enrollment, badge program policy, and 30/60/90-day checks. SLA: ensure offer-to-first-day comms within 2 hours and benefits packet within 24 hours.
- IT/Platform: SSO and baseline account provisioning. SLA: skeleton account within 6 hours, process standard RAFs within 24 hours.
- Team Leads: local onboarding, skill assessment, badge nominations. SLA: complete first-week checklist and nominate badges by day 60.
- Security: review any request that requests production-level roles. SLA: 72-hour review window for elevated requests.

Escalation path
1. If a provisioning request misses SLA, page IT on-call via #it-provisioning and create a ticket in the provisioning queue.
2. If access is denied unexpectedly, Team Lead and People Ops must collaborate within 8 business hours to resolve or request temporary JIT.
3. If benefits enrollment fails, People Ops escalates to Payroll (Finance) within 2 business days.

Audit, compliance, and recordkeeping
- All access provisioning and badge events are recorded in the onboarding system with timestamps and approvers.
- Quarterly audit runs: People Ops + Security verify that badge-to-access mappings are honored and remove stale privileges.
- Retention: access records retained for 3 years.

Review cadence and continuous improvement
- People Ops will run a monthly provisioning health check (MTTR, SLA compliance, common failure modes).
- A semi-annual working group (People Ops, IT, Security, Platform, two Team Leads) will propose adjustments to thresholds, badge criteria, and benefit triggers.

Common scenarios and guidance (FAQ)
Q: New joiner needs immediate production access for a critical fix.
A: Use JIT request flow. Team Lead must submit a high-priority RAF with a remediation justification; Security must approve. JIT access is time-boxed and logged.

Q: Internal transfer to a different team — what changes?
A: Submit an internal transfer event in HRIS. People Ops triggers re-onboarding: revokes team-specific privileges, provisions new team baseline, and restarts the 60-day badge nomination window for team-specific badges.

Q: I missed the benefits enrollment window.
A: Contact People Ops immediately; exceptions are handled case-by-case and may require special enrollment requests to carriers.

Appendix A: Role badge nomination checklist (Team Lead)
- [ ] Confirm local dev environment + first PR merged
- [ ] Security baseline training completed
- [ ] Runbook or feature doc authored
- [ ] Mentoring assignments (if Mentor & Onboarder)
- Submit nomination via People Ops portal -> Attach evidence links (PRs, runbooks, training completion)

Appendix B: Example audit query (SQL-like pseudocode)
- SELECT user, badge, granted_at, approver FROM onboarding_events WHERE badge = 'System Owner' AND granted_at >= '2026-01-01';
